facts.raw_span: a six-year history of a painless swelling in the left supraclavicular region
gradually enlarged from the size of an almond to that of a lime
no history of trauma, fever, or systemic illness
no weakness, numbness, or loss of function in the upper limb
a 4.0-cm diameter, round, firm, non-tender mass in the left supraclavicular area
mobile in the medio-lateral direction
ultrasound showed a superficial heterogeneous round cystic mass measuring 47 × 33 mm
well-defined smooth margins and multiple intralesional septa
its lower border lay adjacent to the subclavian artery and its medial border abutted the carotid artery and external jugular vein
ultrasound was interpreted as a branchial cleft cyst with an atypical location
fine needle aspiration was performed, and the cystogram findings corroborated this diagnosis
scheduled for surgical excision of the suspected branchial cleft cyst

concepts.why: The patient's presentation of a painless swelling in the left supraclavicular region, combined with ultrasound findings of a heterogeneous round cystic mass with well-defined smooth margins and multiple intralesional septa, is consistent with a branchial cleft cyst.
Although less likely, the patient's presentation could also be consistent with a thyroglossal duct cyst, given the location and characteristics of the mass.
The patient's presentation of a firm, non-tender mass could also be consistent with a benign tumor, although this is less likely given the ultrasound findings.
The patient's presentation of a firm, non-tender mass could also be consistent with a lipoma, although this is less likely given the ultrasound findings.
Although less likely, the patient's presentation could also be consistent with an abscess, given the location and characteristics of the mass.
The patient's presentation of no weakness, numbness, or loss of function in the upper limb makes cellulitis a possible, although less likely, diagnosis.
The patient's presentation of a heterogeneous round cystic mass could also be consistent with a cystic hygroma, although this is less likely given the location and ultrasound findings.
The patient's presentation of a firm, non-tender mass could also be consistent with a dermoid cyst, although this is less likely given the ultrasound findings.

rationales.F01: Painless swelling in the left supraclavicular region is more typical of a branchial cleft cyst than other conditions.
rationales.F03: Absence of trauma, fever, or systemic illness makes an abscess or cellulitis less likely.
rationales.F05: A firm, non-tender mass in the left supraclavicular area is consistent with a branchial cleft cyst or other benign conditions.
rationales.F07: Ultrasound findings of a heterogeneous round cystic mass with well-defined smooth margins and multiple intralesional septa are highly suggestive of a branchial cleft cyst.
rationales.F08: The presence of multiple intralesional septa is a characteristic feature of branchial cleft cysts.
rationales.F10: The ultrasound interpretation of a branchial cleft cyst with an atypical location strongly supports this diagnosis.
rationales.F11: Fine needle aspiration and cystogram findings corroborating the diagnosis of a branchial cleft cyst provide strong evidence for this condition.
